content.title: About
content.content: Tilapia is a freshwater fish from the cichlid family, widely farmed in aquaculture. The NFS (1117) strain is a popular commercial variety known for its mild flavor, tender white flesh, and low fat content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tilapia is one of the fastest‑growing farmed fish, reaching market size in 6‑8 months.
Unlike many marine species, tilapia can thrive on plant‑based feeds, reducing production costs.
It can be raised in both fresh and slightly brackish water conditions.
The flesh is virtually boneless, making it convenient for children and people with chewing difficulties.
Tilapia is featured in cuisines worldwide, from Asian to Mediterranean dishes.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Tilapia contains less fat than many other fish, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100‑g serving provides about 20 g of high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which support energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Tilapia provides phosphorus, selenium, and potassium, important for bones, antioxidant protection, and blood pressure regulation.

items.title: Moderate omega‑3
items.content: While lower in omega‑3 than fatty fish, tilapia still contributes to cardiovascular health.

items.title: Contaminants from low‑quality feed
items.content: If raised on feed containing excessive chemicals, harmful residues may accumulate in the flesh.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, including tilapia.

items.title: Low omega‑3 content
items.content: For those seeking high omega‑3 levels, tilapia is not a substitute for fatty fish like salmon.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Tilapia can be baked, grilled, steamed, or poached. It pairs well with lemon, herbs, garlic, and light sauces. Boneless fillets are easy to cube for salads, soups, and tacos.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh tilapia refrigerated at 0‑2 °C and use within 2 days. Frozen fillets store at –18 °C for up to 6 months. Rinse and pat dry before cooking.
